display.title: The Agunah Is Saved, Part 2
display.summary_short: The Alter Rebbe's mysterious instruction comes true in Vilna, and Reb Meir Refoels learns what a single mitzvah is worth when he pays a fortune for one tzitzis string.
display.summary_long: After the song, the storyteller recaps how the Alter Rebbe sent a woman whose husband had vanished three years earlier to Reb Meir Refoels, the head of the Vilna community and a strong opponent of the Chassidim, and how she refused to leave. He explains why many Jews were wary of Chassidus at first and how those who looked into it found more joy and love in serving Hashem. Then the police chief calls Reb Meir about Jewish prisoners passing through on the way to Siberia. One prisoner has the missing husband's name; the woman identifies him, and Reb Meir arranges his release in exchange for a get, freeing her to remarry. Amazed at the Alter Rebbe's foresight, Reb Meir begins to respect the Chassidim and later becomes a Chassid himself. A second story follows: on a business trip Reb Meir's tzitzis becomes unfit, and he pays a passing peddler all the money he has for one string. When he later visits the Alter Rebbe, the Rebbe returns the money and reveals that the peddler was Eliyahu HaNavi, sent to test him.
display.lesson: A tzaddik sees what others cannot, and a mitzvah is worth more than all the money in the world; whatever we give for Hashem comes back with blessings.

advisories.note: A woman is left an agunah after her husband abandons her; he refuses to return and gives her a get.
Jewish prisoners are being sent to Siberia for lacking residence permits.
